title: Enough compactifiable affine opens
statement:
For a finite-type scheme $X$ over a Noetherian scheme $S$ there is a finite
affine cover $X=\bigcup_{r=1}^mU_r$ whose total intersection is dense in $X$.
If $X\to S$ is separated, each $U_r\to S$ has a projective compactification.

proof.text:
There are finitely many irreducible components of $X$. For any point of
$X$, the affine-neighbourhood lemma (Stacks 01ZX) supplies an affine open
containing that point and all the generic points of those components.
Quasi-compactness selects finitely many such opens. Their total intersection
still contains all generic points and is therefore dense.

Each $U_r$ is affine and its map to $S$ is of finite type. The relative
affine-space immersion lemma (Stacks 04II; [sk-prop-nagata-sketch-zmt])
embeds it as a locally closed subscheme of some $\mathbf A^{n_r}_S$. Its
schematic closure in $\mathbf P^{n_r}_S$ is proper, and
[sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] makes $U_r$ an open in that closure.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a quasi-compact scheme $X$ with finitely many irreducible components
(e.g. $X$ of finite type over a Noetherian scheme $S$) there is a finite
affine cover $X=\bigcup_{r=1}^mU_r$ whose total intersection is dense in $X$.
If $Y$ is quasi-affine and $Y\to S$ is locally of finite type and
quasi-compact, then $Y\to S$ has a compactification
([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]); this applies to each $U_r\to S$ when $X$ is of
finite type over a quasi-separated $S$.

proof.text:
For any point of $X$, the affine-neighbourhood lemma (Stacks 01ZX, in its
case of finitely many irreducible components) supplies an affine open
containing that point and all the generic points of the components.
Quasi-compactness selects finitely many such opens. Their total intersection
still contains all generic points and is therefore dense.

For the second assertion, $Y$ is quasi-affine and locally of finite type
over $S$, so the relative affine-space immersion lemma (Stacks 04II;
[lemma-nagata-zmt-open-immersion-affine-factorization], [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists]) embeds it over $S$ as a locally closed
subscheme of some $\mathbf A^{n}_S$. As $Y\to S$ is quasi-compact, so is the
resulting immersion $Y\to\mathbf P^{n}_S$. Its schematic closure in
$\mathbf P^{n}_S$ is proper over $S$, and [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure]
makes $Y$ an open in that closure. An affine $U_r$ is quasi-affine, its map
to $S$ is locally of finite type, and it is quasi-compact because $U_r$ is
quasi-compact and $S$ is quasi-separated.
